findings.detail: STILL PRESENT, both factual claims confirmed false, now fixed in the docstring. (1) COUNT: `grep -n q_entry self_organize.py` gives six reader sites -- :2320 (route_w's non-grounded else), :2567 (seed_key's body; :2564 is the def line the docstring cited), :2591, :2597, :4019 (`fab.q_entry.in_features`, a shape read in fab_logits) and :9156 (the SPECIALIZATION probe) -- against the docstring's 'exactly three readers'. (2) ARM: `awk` over :2584-2597 prints `if s.grounded:` at indent 8 and `_hlg = (...)` at :2595 also at indent 8, so `_hlg` is evaluated AFTER that if closes, on BOTH branches, gated only on `s.halt_on`. FAB_HALT is not a dropped arm -- .rework/census.json verdicts it `keep` while ROUTE_GROUNDED and FAB_DERIVE_IDS are both `drop`; src/fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.halt is Lever(True, ...); src/fabric/api.py::build reads it and writes counters['fab.halt'] (measured 0 at FAB_HALT=0, 1 at FAB_HALT=1). So a q_entry reader IS reached at the shipped ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 on the ported soc walk whenever FAB_HALT=0. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES, BUT THE VERIFIER'S RESCUE ARGUMENT IS ITSELF NARROWER THAN CLAIMED and I did not adopt it as written: it says the halt column 'changes neither the ranking nor the EMA rate' because ground_update renormalises. That holds per ROW, not per batch. c[:, :N] = alpha_b * p_b with alpha_b = S_b/(S_b + exp(halt_b)) depending on q_entry, and ground_update takes `_wm = w.mean(0)` (:2410) BEFORE `_share = _iv / _iv.sum().clamp_min(1e-9)` (:2414), so a per-row factor that varies across rows survives the mean. Replaying :2598-2603 into :2410-2414 over 400 draws at B=8, N=32, FAB_CENT_TOPK=8: top-k SET differs in 137/400, per-index rate differs in 400/400, max rate delta 0.056; at B=1, 0/400. The drop is instead carried by two facts I established: ground_update's body is entirely under `with torch.no_grad():` (:2404) and `c` is consumed by nothing else on the ported walk (:2603 only; `if s.loop_soc:` at :2618 returns at :2694; later reads of `c` start at :2703, inside the transition arm Q-FAB-1 leaves unported), so q_entry has NO gradient path at EITHER FAB_HALT setting; and the loop's own halt-off arm pins the halt logit to `torch.full((h.size(0), 1), -1e4)` (:2628) rather than deriving it, so :2597 is the pre-halt-lever remnant and a faithful FAB_HALT=0 port takes :2628's form. Two supporting citations also corrected: the 'never gradiented -> ctrl, q_entry' measurement (:9141, audit loop at :7085) was taken at the shipped ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 AND the shipped FAB_HALT=1 (:1734), so on its own it says nothing about the halt-off arm; and the two armed-but-inert ISSUES records are P3-C28 and P3-H30 (now cited by RECORD ID, since that file's line numbers have already moved once -- the numbers 1594-1595 / 1789-1790 used in .rework/audits/close_fabric_ckpt.json land on P3-C26 and P3-H28 instead). Finally the return trigger is widened from 'the same commit that ports a non-grounded entry router' to ANY LIVE CONSUMER of the pre-loop entry distribution `c` -- a literal port of :2597 keeping the derived halt logit, or any use of `c` beyond ground_update's no-grad EMA -- because each of those puts q_entry back on a gradient path. No code changed: build's allocation and state_dict's ten-name list already agree (modules eemb, edec, q_route, hproj, halt_key, norm, nov_proj plus A, B, halt_b; pop.parameters() returns 20 tensors at both FAB_HALT arms).

Both halves are false: there are SIX reader sites, and :2597 is on BOTH branches (gated on s.halt_on alone), so at ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 with FAB_HALT=0 -- a KEEP lever -- one reader IS reached on the walk this tree ports. The records it meant are P3-C28 (line 1602) and P3-H30 (line 1797). As a closed report it is arguably history rather than a live claim, but it is the document a future reader will follow back from D13, so it needs at minimum an appended correction note.
